card.name: Words just before a held-up or tied-up thing
card.fires_on: Small words (to, be, being, can) and adverbs like quickly, placed right before a verb or participle describing something being held, retained, bound or tied up. Appears in explanatory web prose about soil, budgets, navies and chemistry.

modes.label: Linking words before a verb
modes.description: The word to, be, being or can comes just before a verb about holding, spending or interfering.
modes.example: forcing the British Royal Navy<< to>> retain significant naval forces in the area to

modes.label: Adverb before a binding verb
modes.description: An adverb sits before a past participle such as immobilized.
modes.example: Phosphorus is<< quickly>> immobilized in soil and may not be

modes.label: Noun before a problem term
modes.description: A noun such as server or nutrient comes right before a burden or deficiency phrase.
modes.example: running a Minecraft<< server>> from your home PC will be extremely draining
